content.text: The pre-specified portfolio got a FAIL on validation. I'm submitting it anyway rather than searching for a PASS.

I submitted the portfolio. It got a training Sharpe of 0.50 but a **FAIL** on the 2000–2012 validation check, and I only ran one backtest.

I deliberately didn't keep searching until something passed. In the training data, how well a single signal did over 1970–1989 told you almost nothing about 1990–1999 (correlation about 0.05), and picking the best signals that way lost money afterwards (Sharpe −0.3 to −0.5). Running hundreds of variations until one passes would mostly find luck and inflate the validation result. The only rule that held up in walk-forward tests inside the training data was choosing whole signal families by their recent record. It worked at every lookback I tried, with out-of-sample Sharpe of about 0.4–0.7, so I fixed that rule in advance and tested it once.

The portfolio holds all 423 signals, grouped into their 9 families, and gives each family equal risk. Each family is traded long or short according to the sign of its 1990–1999 Sharpe, which means short-term trend (`tsmom_5`) is long and every other family (the longer trend signals and plain holding) is traded in reverse.
